assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 (glucose-dependent insulin secretion, appetite and gastric effects) and led to incretin therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Originality, clarity and very large clinical and societal impact make this the strongest case on the list.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, receptor action, translation) and Mojsov (peptide identification and active-form characterization) form a plausible trio. Knudsen's industrial drug-development role is substantial but sits more as translation. The credited list omits other early contributors I recall (for example Habener), so the configuration is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Decades of mechanistic work and multiple approved, widely used drugs with large outcome trials; confirmation is extensive and independent. Timing is ripe given the clinical impact of semaglutide and tirzepatide.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Knudsen and uncredited early contributors is contested, and I have not independently verified the priority claims.
Whether the committee prefers recognizing physiology versus drug development is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave a general method for causal, millisecond-precision control of defined cell types, reshaping circuit neuroscience and extending to cardiology and vision restoration. It is an invention-type discovery with clear originality and a huge methodological impact on physiology, directly relevant to how motor and other circuits are dissected.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth established their use in neurons and in behavior. Bamberg (early work with Nagel), Boyden and Miesenböck also have strong claims, so a three-person cap forces painful exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of validation across thousands of laboratories, with first clinical applications emerging (optogenetic vision restoration). Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Crowded priority picture (Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenböck, Zemelman-type contributions) makes the three-name configuration contestable.
Clinical benefit is still early, which may matter to some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and established a new therapeutic modality; the concept, costimulatory design and clinical proof of principle are clear and important.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL), Sadelain (CAR design with costimulation, preclinical work) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T cells) are credible. Eshhar's foundational chimeric-receptor concept is not among the credited names, which weakens a fair configuration as listed.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation in hematologic cancers; limited efficacy in solid tumors and toxicity and cost remain, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Unresolved credit for the original chimeric receptor concept and for second-generation designs.
Whether Rosenberg's broader adoptive cell therapy work is best recognized as part of this discovery or separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR and mTOR as the central regulator of cell growth and nutrient responses, a conserved pathway touching metabolism, ageing, cancer and immunology. The concept is original, clean and broadly foundational.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast and framed its role in growth control; Schreiber's work on rapamycin and FKBP12 and Sabatini's identification of mTOR complexes and nutrient sensing are strong follow-on contributions. Hall is the clear anchor; the other two are a judgment call versus others (for example Heitman, Hall's co-discoverers, and Sabatini's controversial standing I cannot resolve).
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed across systems, with clinical use of rapalogs; the pathway interpretation has been refined but is stable.
uncertainties: Allocation beyond Hall is uncertain and relies on my recollection of priority.
Rapamycin pharmacology predates TOR and may complicate the narrative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeted inhibition of the BCR-ABL kinase converted chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal to a manageable disease and defined the paradigm of kinase-inhibitor cancer therapy. The impact is large and clear.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development at Ciba-Geigy), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof of principle) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are a natural trio. Rowley and others contributed upstream to the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion, which is outside the credited names and could be argued as a precondition.
assessment.maturity: Decades of survival data and independent confirmation; recognition is mature and arguably overdue relative to its Lasker recognition.
uncertainties: The prize may be seen as drug development rather than discovery of a basic mechanism.
Upstream credit for the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion lies outside the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed how the ER communicates folding stress to the nucleus (IRE1-HAC1/XBP1 signaling), a fundamental principle of cellular quality control with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the clearly identified discoverers of the pathway; the two-person configuration is clean. Other contributors (for example Ron and Harding on PERK, or Sidrauskas/Cox) are not credited and would need separate consideration.
assessment.maturity: Well established across yeast and mammals with a stable conceptual framework; therapeutic translation is still limited, which makes the clinical impact less direct than other candidates.
uncertainties: Fair treatment of the PERK/ATF6 branches and their discoverers is not resolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identification and its loss in narcolepsy established a molecular basis for wake stability, and led to orexin receptor antagonists for insomnia. It is a clear case of a neuropeptide system linked to a human disease.
assessment.attribution: Yanagisawa and Sakurai discovered orexin and its receptors; the link to canine and human narcolepsy came from Mignot and Yanagisawa. De Lecea and Kilduff reported hypocretin independently, which creates a simultaneous-discovery problem and a five-person set that cannot all be recognized.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated, with approved drugs, although agonists for narcolepsy are still in clinical development. Timing is reasonable, not urgent.
uncertainties: Credit among the independent hypocretin and orexin discoverers is genuinely contested.
Autoimmune etiology of human narcolepsy is incompletely resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune and interferon responses, with consequences for infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and ageing. It is a clear, original mechanism with broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP; Barber identified STING. Other credited names are coauthors rather than lead conceptual contributors in my view. Burdette and Vance on cyclic dinucleotide sensing are not credited, which may matter.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and mechanistically stable, but clinical translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) is not yet established, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Allocation among Chen, Barber and uncredited cyclic dinucleotide researchers is unresolved.
